title: George Washington and Bill of Rights

hint.text: Tippe den Lautsprecher unter dem Bild an, wenn du den Text noch einmal hören willst.

atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody rate='90%'> George Washington was born on the 22nd of February 1732. He was involved in the Revolutionary War and together with other British colonists fought against Great Britain. In 1789, George Washington became the first President of the United States of America. He was president of the USA for 2 terms, a total of 8 years. George Washington died on the 14th of December 1799 after he suffered from a throat infection. Because he played a big role in the founding of the United States, he's also called “Father of his Country”.</prosody>

atoms.text: Now that the former British colonies were independent of Great Britain, they needed to create new laws for themselves. First, the Constitution was created. This document defines laws and rules for the government. An important document that was added to the Constitution is called the Bill of Rights. The Bill of Rights explained 10 basic freedoms and rights that all American citizens had. These rights were written in 1791 and are also called amendments.

atoms.a: How many amendments are in the “Bill of Rights”?
atoms.sound: How many amendments are in the Bill of Rights?

atoms.a: When were the “Bill of Rights” created?
atoms.sound: When were the Bill of Rights created?

atoms.a: What do the “Bill of Rights” define?

atoms.text: Here are some examples from the “Bill of Rights”:

example.a: 1. Amendment: </br> Freedom of speech and press are protected. People are also allowed to come together in public for peaceful protests and choose their own religion.
example.sound: The first amendment says that freedom of speech and press are protected. People are also allowed to come together in public for peaceful protests and choose their own religion.

example.a: 2. Amendment: </br> People are allowed to bear arms.
example.sound: The second amendment says that people are allowed to bear arms.

hint.sound: to bear arms <voice voiceLang='de' voice='m3'>bedeutet Waffen tragen.</voice>

example.a: 9. Amendment: </br> The “Bill of Rights” only includes the 10 most basic rights. That doesn't mean that other rights aren't valid and important too.
example.sound: The ninth amendment says that the Bill of Rights only includes the 10 most basic rights. That doesn't mean that other rights aren't valid and important too.
